summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini Robotics 2, a new family of three robotics models (a VLA, an embodied-reasoning model, and an on-device VLA) that add whole-body humanoid control, advanced dexterous manipulation, multi-robot collaboration, and fast on-device adaptation to new robot bodies.

mechanisms.reason: The model achieves, for the first time, full whole-body control of humanoid robots rather than only upper-body table-top manipulation, a stated step change in task scope.
mechanisms.quote: For the first time, our model can now control entire humanoid robots, translating intent into intelligent whole-body control.

mechanisms.reason: A dedicated on-device VLA model is optimized to run locally on robotic hardware rather than in the datacenter, pushing inference to the edge.
mechanisms.quote: Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 is built specifically to handle these constraints — it is our most-efficient vision-language-action model (VLA) optimized to run locally on robotic devices.

practices.reason: Teams building embodied or agentic robotics systems should evaluate the new whole-body control, multi-step task reasoning, and improved human-proximity safety behavior before relying on them, since results are the lab's own and only in early access.
practices.quote: It observes the room, reasons about the steps needed to complete the task, coordinates with the VLA to carry out the actions, and tracks progress until the task is done.

practices.reason: The new ASIMOV-Agentic benchmark for agentic safety orchestration and refusal of unsafe tool calls is a transferable measurement approach teams could adapt for their own embodied-agent safety testing.
practices.quote: We’re introducing ASIMOV-Agentic , a new benchmark for agentic safety orchestration and uncertainty resolution.

practices.reason: Multi-robot collaboration is described as a new capability but without enough architectural detail for a team to implement the coordination pattern themselves.
practices.quote: we are introducing multi-robot collaboration. This enables different types of robots to communicate and work together to solve complex workflows a single robot could not do alone.
